title: What If 24 Rabbits Were Released on a Whole Continent?

scenes.text: What if 24 rabbits were set loose on a whole continent? Australia found out.
They were released on Christmas Day 1859, for hunting. Seven years later, over 14,000 had been shot on that one estate.
By the 1880s they had spread across most of southeastern Australia, at times advancing about 100 kilometers a year.
A fence over 3,200 kilometers long was built to stop them. It slowed them, but it did not end the invasion.
Myxomatosis in the 1950s cut their numbers at first. Then the survivors became resistant.
Today there are still more than 150 million, costing Australia over 200 million dollars a year.

description:
What if 24 rabbits were released on a whole continent?
In 1859, Thomas Austin let 24 rabbits go in Victoria. They spread across most of southeastern Australia within decades, and over 150 million remain today.
